title: Vectors & Forces — every example, by concept
note: Artifact-level mind-map: every artifact placed heuristically from concept + tier + reading order. y = concept_order (timeline); x morphs from a single column (order) to concept clusters (x_spread).

concepts.act: Act I — what a vector is
concepts.truth: Before a vector, a where: three axes, an origin, an agreed order (x, y, z).

concepts.act: Act I — what a vector is
concepts.truth: A vector is a step, not a place - a direction and a length you can carry anywhere.

concepts.act: Act I — what a vector is
Act I — what a vector is
concepts.truth: Divide by length and every direction gets a unit twin.
a + b is where you land if you walk a then b - tip to tail.
b - a is the arrow of the gap, pointing from here to there.
A scalar is a volume knob for a direction - same line, new length.
the dot product is how much two directions agree — and here, agreeing is mercy
projection is the part of you that lives along someone else's line
the cross product is the turn left over when two directions disagree
a field is force that has decided to be everywhere at once
Every bubble leaves along the vector you point.
Only the part along the motion does work: W = F*d*cos(t).
Resistance grows with speed: F = -b*v.
Gravity applied each frame bends a straight launch into a parabola.
Constant acceleration toward a centre you never reach: a = v2/r.
Every mass pulls every other: F = G*m1*m2/r2.
a spring is honest — it returns exactly what it's given, which is why it keeps time
a pendulum keeps time because the pull back is proportional to how far it's pulled
momentum is motion that refuses to be destroyed, only handed on
every bounce is a tax on a fall
a lever trades force for distance and never gets something for nothing. *(The Calder mobile is this law, drifting — every arm balanced by real weights.)*
wind is air with somewhere to be; the force is in the speed, squared
falling isn't a property of the void; it's a property of the field over it — and the field is a vector you can turn
A force is a vector on a mass: F = m*a.
